title: Stereochemistry in RNA Manufacturing: Signal or Noise?
summary: Meta Description: Why phosphorothioate stereochemistry is becoming a discovery decision in siRNA development, and what it means for potency, cost and scalable manufacturing.
body_markdown:
As RNA therapeutics advance toward larger patient populations and commercial-scale manufacturing, developers are placing greater emphasis on designing molecules that can be manufactured consistently from the outset. Increasingly, this means considering stereochemistry during early discovery as a factor in candidate selection, with a view to supporting seamless scale-up and manufacturing.


If you’re new to phosphorothioate (PS) stereochemistry and want to learn why it matters in RNA manufacturing, read our previous blog on[Building Scalable RNA Manufacturing with Greater Stereochemical Control.](https://www.codexis.com/blogs/building-scalable-rna-manufacturing-with-greater-stereochemical-control/)


Rather than asking how to control stereochemistry during manufacturing, a more important question is emerging: Should stereochemical control begin much earlier? By incorporating stereochemical considerations during discovery and lead optimization, developers can identify candidates that are biologically effective and better suited for robust, scalable manufacturing.
